subject: SIG: Medica - records assertion & evidence for prompt logs and training
messages:
From: Claire Morgan <claire.morgan@medica.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Medica Security Team <sec-questions@medica.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: prompt logs, training on customer data, retention windows

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Medica's security team is working through the SIG questionnaire and we landed on a few follow-ups where we'd like explicit statements and evidence from Redwood:

1) Prompt / request logs: what do you persist by default? Please state retention windows, whether logs are redacted, and who (roles/teams) can access them for troubleshooting.
2) KV/prefix cache behavior: do you ever materialize KV cache or prompt history to durable storage? If so, under what circumstances and retention?
3) Training on customer data: does Redwood ever use customer input (prompts, attachments, outputs) to train or tune models in the hosted offering? If the answer is no, we need a short attestation and any supporting artifacts (policy excerpts, SOC2 evidence).
4) Evidence: we need a small evidence bundle suitable for our SIG submission (config screenshots, policy PDFs, and a short statement). Zip or Drive link is fine.

Can you provide a concise response and evidence pack by EOD Monday? Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Claire
Security Program Manager
Medica Health

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Claire Morgan <claire.morgan@medica.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt logs, training on customer data, retention windows

Claire — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching a short summary (redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf). I can follow up with an evidence bundle by Monday.

1) Prompt / request logs: By default, Redwood retains request/response traces for short-term operational purposes (debugging, alert triage) for 14 days in the hosted environment. Logs are redacted for obvious secrets (we redact common secret patterns and provide customer-configurable redact rules). Access is limited to SRE/ops staff with privileged access; access is audited and requires justification.

2) KV/prefix cache: KV cache is in-memory and per-inference-session for hosted endpoints. We do not flush KV cache to durable object storage as part of normal serving. In exceptional maintenance workflows (migration, cluster reprovision) a transient snapshot may be taken to speed restart; such snapshots are encrypted, retained only for the maintenance window, and deleted within 72 hours. We will provide an architecture diagram snippet in the evidence pack.

3) Training on customer data: Redwood does not use customer prompts, files, or outputs from the hosted product to train or improve baseline models unless a customer explicitly opts in and signs a separate data-use agreement. Dedicated and Private deployments do not feed customer data into our central training pipeline. This is covered in our data use policy and SOC 2 controls — see attached summary and we will include the SOC 2 attestation excerpt in the evidence bundle.

4) Evidence: attaching a short one-page summary now. I will compile screenshots (audit log snippet, retention config UI), the SOC 2 excerpt, and an operations statement into a single zip and share via Drive by Monday EOD.

If you'd like a short recorded statement or signed attestation, let me know and I can escalate to legal.

— Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf)

From: Claire Morgan <claire.morgan@medica.com>

Date: Fri, 19 Feb 2027 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt logs, training on customer data, retention windows

Thanks — that helps a lot. Two quick clarifications before you compile the pack:

• For the 14 day logs: are those logs accessible to engineers beyond SRE if a legal or security request comes in? We need to understand escalation procedures and role separation.
• For KV snapshots during maintenance: can you confirm whether snapshots ever include unredacted prompt text or attachments? If so, are they redacted before persistence?

If it's easier to answer inline in the evidence doc, that's fine.

Appreciate it,
Claire

Kimberly / Neha — looping you in. Medica wants: (a) explicit statement on engineer access / role separation for the 14-day logs, and (b) confirmation whether maintenance snapshots ever contain unredacted prompt text/attachments and, if they do, how they are redacted and deleted.

Can you prepare a short operations statement (1) listing the roles and the escalation process, and (2) a short note on maintenance snapshot handling plus any config UI screenshots we can include in the evidence bundle? Thanks — I need to send the final bundle to Medica by EOD today.

— Sergio

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>

Cc: Medica Security Team <sec-questions@medica.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 14:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: prompt logs, training on customer data, retention windows — Evidence pack attached

Claire — attaching the evidence bundle we compiled for Medica. Contents and short authoritative statements below. Drive link and HubSpot record included for traceability.

Attachments: medica-sig-evidence-pack.zip (contains: audited-retention-policy-2027-02.pdf, ops-access-statement.pdf, kv-snapshot-process.pdf, audit-log-screenshot.png)

Summary (authoritative statements):
• Prompt/request logs: Hosted request and response traces are retained for 14 days for operational troubleshooting. Logs are redacted for common secret patterns; customers can configure additional redact rules. Access to logs requires an approved request and is restricted to SRE/Platform Operations and a small set of authorized engineers for emergency incident response. All access is logged and reviewed quarterly. (See ops-access-statement.pdf)
• KV/prefix cache: The KV/prefix cache used during inference is in-memory and scoped to the serving process. We do not persist KV cache to durable object storage during normal operation. In exceptional maintenance workflows we may create encrypted, transient snapshots to accelerate restart; those snapshots are reviewed, encrypted at rest, and irreversibly deleted within 72 hours. Snapshots never persist unredacted customer attachments — attachments are stored only in customer-managed object stores for Private deployments or in isolated buckets for Dedicated customers and are excluded from snapshots. (See kv-snapshot-process.pdf)
• Training on customer data: Redwood does not use customer prompts, attachments, or outputs from the hosted product to train or fine-tune our public model fleet unless a customer provides explicit opt-in via a signed data-use agreement. Dedicated and Private customers retain full control — data never flows into our central training pipelines. We have included the SOC 2 excerpt and the policy page in the bundle. (See audited-retention-policy-2027-02.pdf)

If you want a signed attestation on company letterhead, I can coordinate that with Legal and Security — please confirm and we'll produce it within 48 hours.

HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/medica-record-98765
Drive folder (evidence): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-medica-sig-evidence

Let me know if you need anything else. Happy to hop on a brief call to walk through the artifacts.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
